newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: INTERVIEW-LION GOES UPMARKET WITH STELLA.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW-LION GOES UPMARKET WITH STELLA.

text.p: Lion Nathan's decision to distribute Stella Artois through Lion Breweries was designed to cash in on the trend towards upmarket beers, chief executive Douglas Myers said on Thursday.
The move was not designed as a spoiler for its domestic competitor, DB Group, which brews Heineken under licence, Myers told Reuters.
Stella will join Lion's premium stable led by Steinlager, Speights Distinction Ale and Guinness, which Lion brews under licence in Christchurch.

"Stella is a premium brand, Heineken is a premium brand," Myers told Reuters. "I think they will be positive for each other as Heineken has been positive for Steinlager, because it's directed consumers' attention to a range and style of products that traditional beer drinkers previously didn't see," he said.
Heineken was seen as an international brand but Stella, from an image standpoint, was a more complex proposition, Myers said.
Depending on the retailer, Stella will sell for around NZ$24.95 a dozen, down from the current NZ$40 through Lion's 50 percent owned New Zealand Wines and Spirits.
The move keeps Stella's position at the top end and effectively surrounds Heineken in pricing.
Lion's flagship, Steinlager, retails for around $17 a dozen and Heineken, at DB's insistance, is not allowed to be sold for anthing less than NZ$19.95.

"Consumers are voting with their feet - they are moving from quantity to quality. The better portfolio of premium brands that we've got the better we're going to meet those needs," Lion Breweries national marketing manager Kevin Kenrick told Reuters.
About 15,000 cases of Stella sold domestically last year.
Kenrick said Lion would aim to grow that to two or three times that size, but not at the expense of Steinlager.
"We want to enhance our position rather than cannibalise our position," he said.
Lion Nathan, which has enjoyed a strong erally in recent weeks, closed today at NZ$4.04, down one cent.
